desc.k17449: Measures calcitriol, the active 1,25-dihydroxy form of vitamin D, to investigate disorders of calcium, the parathyroid glands, bone or kidney function. It is used in selected situations such as kidney failure, PTH disorders and vitamin D-resistant rickets.
desc.k17928: 17-OH progesterone is a precursor in the production of cortisol and adrenal androgens. It is used in screening for congenital adrenal hyperplasia and in investigating hormonal disorders, including hirsutism, irregular cycles or infertility; interpretation depends on age, sex and the phase of the menstrual cycle.
desc.k17445: ACE is an enzyme involved in regulating blood pressure, and its production may increase in tissue affected by sarcoidosis. The test helps in diagnosing sarcoidosis and in monitoring its course in people with a confirmed diagnosis.
desc.k17461: Methylmalonic acid rises when there is not enough vitamin B12 for normal metabolism and can help detect a deficiency even when B12 is borderline. It is also used in diagnosing methylmalonic acidaemia and in monitoring treatment or metabolic control.
desc.k17376: Uric acid is a breakdown product of purines that is removed mainly by the kidneys. Measuring it helps assess gout, investigate or monitor kidney stones and check uric acid in patients receiving chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
desc.k17501: Measures uric acid excretion in a 24-hour urine collection to assess purine metabolism, particularly when the blood level is raised. It is used in gout, recurrent kidney stones, kidney disease and during follow-up after chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
desc.k17377: Measures uric acid in a single urine sample to complete the assessment when the blood level is high. It may be used in gout, kidney disease, recurrent stones and during follow-up of patients after chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
desc.k18244: Measuring valproic acid helps monitor a medicine with a narrow therapeutic range. It is used at the start of treatment, after a dose change, when the medicine is not working well enough or toxicity is suspected, to support individualised treatment.
desc.k17912: Vanillylmandelic acid is a product of catecholamine metabolism that is excreted in the urine. Measuring it in a 24-hour urine collection helps diagnose and monitor treatment of catecholamine-secreting tumours, particularly phaeochromocytoma and neuroblastoma, as well as assess noradrenaline metabolism in certain clinical settings.
desc.k17585: Measures total bile acids in serum to assess disorders of the liver and bile ducts. It is important in diagnosing and monitoring intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy; the description mentions increases in hepatitis, cirrhosis or obstruction of bile flow, and its use in monitoring certain treatments.
desc.k17683: The profile quantifies long-chain fatty acids, omega-3/omega-6 and their ratios to assess metabolic and nutritional status. It is used when peroxisomal disorders are suspected, during specialised nutrition, or when monitoring dietary restrictions and the treatment of essential fatty acid deficiency.
desc.k17913: ACTH is a pituitary hormone that stimulates the adrenal glands to produce cortisol. Measuring it together with cortisol helps distinguish the causes of cortisol excess or deficiency, including Cushing's disease, adrenal insufficiency, hypopituitarism and ectopic ACTH production.
desc.k17457: Adiponectin links the activity of fat tissue with insulin sensitivity, glucose metabolism and inflammation. A doctor may include the measurement when assessing obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes or cardiovascular risk, and when monitoring interventions for metabolic health.
desc.k17943: ADH, or vasopressin, helps regulate water in the body and the concentration of urine. The measurement is used in investigating diabetes insipidus, SIADH, hyponatraemia or increased urination, and in assessing disorders of fluid and electrolyte balance.
desc.k18176: AFP is used to help assess and monitor tumours of the liver, testes and ovaries. It may also be included in prenatal screening together with other markers, and in monitoring chronic liver disease.
desc.k17380: Measures albumin, the main protein in the blood, which is made in the liver. It helps assess liver and kidney disease, malabsorption or malnutrition, and is used for nutritional monitoring of hospitalised patients or in pre-operative assessment.
desc.k17417: Measures albumin excreted in a 24-hour urine collection to help detect kidney damage early, particularly in diabetes and high blood pressure. It is also used to monitor treatment, together with creatinine, urea and markers of control of the underlying disease.
desc.k17490: Albumin in the second morning urine helps detect kidney damage early, particularly in people with diabetes or high blood pressure. The result is reported as an albumin/creatinine ratio and is used to monitor treatment together with markers of kidney function and of the underlying disease.
desc.k17465: Aldolase is an enzyme of glucose metabolism found in significant amounts in muscle. Measuring it helps investigate and monitor muscle damage, including myopathies, polymyositis and dermatomyositis; increases can also occur in other diseases, so it needs to be assessed alongside other findings.
desc.k17372: The panel measures specific IgE to a group of allergens, mainly inhaled ones, to help find the trigger after an allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result may indicate sensitisation without clinical allergy, so results are matched with symptoms and an allergy assessment.
desc.k19247: The panel measures specific IgE to milk, several of its proteins and gluten to help identify the trigger after allergic or anaphylactic reactions. The result shows possible sensitisation and is interpreted together with symptoms and an allergy assessment.
desc.k17373: Food panel 30 measures specific IgE to a group of foods and food ingredients to help identify the cause of allergic reactions. A positive result shows sensitisation that must be matched with symptoms; a negative result does not completely rule out allergy, and interpretation is a matter for the allergist.
desc.k17561: The 20-allergen food panel examines the IgE response to the listed foods to help investigate food allergy. It is done on a blood sample, and the description highlights that it can also be used in children; results relate to the individual allergens included in the panel.
desc.k17381: Measures alpha-1 antitrypsin, a protective protein made in the liver that limits the action of damaging enzymes in the lungs. It helps investigate emphysema at an early age or liver damage in childhood/adolescence, and assess close relatives of people with a documented deficiency.
desc.k17382: Measures total amylase to help diagnose and monitor pancreatic disease, mainly acute pancreatitis and sometimes chronic pancreatitis. Because the test includes both the pancreatic and salivary gland isoenzymes without distinguishing between them, it is sometimes also used when salivary gland disease is suspected.
desc.k17378: ALT is an enzyme found mainly in liver cells and is used to detect and monitor damage to them. It is measured during routine check-ups or when liver disease is suspected, including viral hepatitis, usually together with AST, ALP, GGT and bilirubin.
desc.k18248: Measuring aluminium helps assess exposure to and accumulation of this metal, particularly in industrial workers and patients on haemodialysis. The description links raised levels to impaired kidney excretion and chronic toxicity; the result is interpreted together with the exposure history.
desc.k17624: Measures aluminium excreted in a 24-hour urine collection to assess exposure to or accumulation of the metal, particularly in industrial work and in patients on haemodialysis. The description also mentions its use in monitoring treatment of accumulation, with interpretation based on kidney function and exposure history.
desc.k17321: Measures specific IgE to Ambrosia elatior (w1) to investigate sensitisation to this allergen. A positive result is assessed together with symptoms after contact, because sensitisation does not necessarily mean clinical allergy; a negative result does not completely rule it out.
desc.k21317: AMH helps assess ovarian reserve and the response of the ovaries during infertility investigations or assisted reproduction. It is also used in selected assessments of PCOS and testicular function, and in monitoring granulosa cell tumours that secrete this hormone.
desc.k17480: Measures pancreatic amylase, a carbohydrate-digesting enzyme made in the pancreas. The description links the test to suspected acute pancreatitis when there is severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting or loss of appetite.
desc.k17460: The panel measures amino acids in plasma to identify build-ups or deficiencies linked to inborn errors of metabolism. It is also used when acquired nutritional, liver, kidney, endocrine or neurological disorders that may alter amino acid balance are suspected.
desc.k17612: Measures ammonia in the blood to assess disorders of its removal, including liver disease, hepatic encephalopathy and urea cycle defects. It may also be used to monitor ammonia-lowering treatment or in selected metabolic investigations.
desc.k17270: The test measures specific IgE to amoxicillin, allergen C204, to help investigate allergic or anaphylactic reactions to this medicine. A positive result must be matched with the clinical history, because sensitisation does not necessarily equal allergy, and a negative result does not rule it out.
desc.k17269: The test measures specific IgE to ampicillin, allergen C203, to help investigate an allergic or anaphylactic reaction to the medicine. A positive result may indicate sensitisation only, and a negative result does not completely rule out allergy; the final assessment also relies on the history and clinical signs.
desc.k17727: Looks for antinuclear antibodies to help diagnose autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren's syndrome. The test is used when symptoms raise a suspicion of autoimmunity, and the result is considered alongside the person's clinical assessment.
desc.k17541: Looks for antinuclear antibodies using a HEp-2 cell substrate to support the diagnosis of systemic connective tissue diseases. It is used when lupus, scleroderma, mixed connective tissue disease or Sjögren's syndrome is suspected; a positive result can also occur in other diseases and needs clinical interpretation.
desc.k17493: Examination of faeces in three preparations looks for starch granules, muscle fibres and fat droplets to assess the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats. It helps investigate enzyme deficiency or intestinal/pancreatic disorders in chronic maldigestion, diarrhoea, fatty stools and weight loss.
desc.k53778: The GUT pathological profile focuses on identifying pathogens and microorganisms in faeces when infection is suspected or there are persistent gastrointestinal complaints. It covers bacteria, fungi and parasites and, for relevant isolates, sensitivity to antimicrobial agents, to help choose further clinical steps.
desc.k17542: The test determines the composition of a urinary stone to help investigate how stones form and recur. The composition can give clues about metabolic disorders, infection or the involvement of medicines, and support the choice of treatment.
desc.k17646: The test measures mineral elements and metals in hair. The laboratory presents it as an indirect look at their accumulation over recent months and at environmental exposure, stressing that interpretation is affected by individual differences and external contamination of the hair.
desc.k17938: Androstenedione is a precursor of testosterone and oestrone, produced by the adrenal glands and the ovaries. Measuring it helps assess adrenal, ovarian or testicular function and may be included in investigating hirsutism, virilisation and polycystic ovary syndrome.
desc.k17821: Measures IgG against Borrelia burgdorferi to assess Lyme disease after exposure to ticks. IgG may appear after several weeks and remain raised for years; the result is reviewed with IgM and symptoms, and an initial positive result may need a confirmatory test.
desc.k17882: Looks for IgM antibodies to Borrelia burgdorferi as part of the serological investigation of Lyme disease after a tick bite. IgM usually becomes detectable after about 2–3 weeks; interpretation takes into account IgG, symptoms and, when needed, confirmatory Western blot testing.
desc.k17733: IgG against cytomegalovirus helps assess past exposure and, together with IgM and avidity, the stage of infection. It is used in pregnancy, before transplantation, in people with weakened immunity and in investigating some congenital abnormalities.
desc.k17734: Measures IgM antibodies to cytomegalovirus to help assess recent infection, reactivation or reinfection. It is used especially in pregnancy, immunosuppression and preparation for transplantation, but IgM alone does not confirm a primary infection and needs to be compared with other tests.
desc.k17860: Measures IgG antibodies against Coxsackie virus to support the assessment of infection when there is prolonged tiredness, fever, palpitations, or heart, joint or gastrointestinal symptoms. The result is interpreted together with IgM, symptoms and other tests; a raised IgG is not assessed on its own.
desc.k17861: IgM antibodies against Coxsackie virus help assess infection when there is fever, tiredness, palpitations, chest pain or bowel complaints. A rise in these antibodies, especially together with IgG, is interpreted in relation to symptoms, clinical signs and other tests.
desc.k17753: IgG against the Epstein–Barr virus capsid antigen (VCA) helps the serological assessment of infection, including infectious mononucleosis. The antibodies appear during infection and may remain for life, so the result is interpreted with clinical signs and other laboratory markers.
desc.k17754: The test looks for IgM antibodies to the Epstein–Barr virus capsid antigen (VCA). It is used to help investigate early infection and infectious mononucleosis; the result is related to the timing of symptoms and to other laboratory and clinical findings.
desc.k18204: Measures total antibodies to HCV to screen for and assess exposure to the hepatitis C virus. A reactive result needs further tests, particularly HCV-RNA, to determine whether the virus is present; in the first weeks, antibodies may not yet be detectable.
desc.k17862: IgA against Helicobacter pylori is a supporting serological test in assessing symptoms of gastritis or ulcer. It can be interpreted together with IgG, but the antibodies may persist after treatment and do not on their own prove an active infection.
desc.k17740: Measures IgG antibodies to Helicobacter pylori, formed in response to infection of the stomach lining. It can help the assessment of gastritis or ulcer symptoms, but the antibodies may reflect a past infection and persist after treatment.
desc.k17838: Specific IgG to HSV-2 can help assess a past infection in selected cases. The test does not establish when the infection occurred; results, especially low-positive ones, may need confirmation. Routine screening of pregnant women without symptoms is not recommended.
desc.k17840: Because of limitations in telling the virus type apart and in distinguishing a new infection from a recurrence, IgM is not recommended for diagnosing herpes; the doctor chooses the test according to the clinical signs.
desc.k17746: Measures IgG to rubella to assess immunity after infection or vaccination, particularly before and in early pregnancy. It may also help assess an infection with rash and swollen lymph nodes, but interpretation requires the clinical context and often IgM or IgG avidity.
desc.k17747: Measures IgM to rubella when a recent infection is suspected, including the assessment of congenital infection. A positive result may be false or related to vaccination; the result requires clinical interpretation and, where appropriate, confirmation. It is not a routine immunity or screening test for pregnant women without symptoms.
desc.k17750: Measures IgG against Toxoplasma gondii to assess contact with the parasite, especially when planning a pregnancy, during pregnancy or in immunosuppression. A single positive IgG does not distinguish a recent infection from a past one; interpretation may require IgM, avidity and repeat measurements.
desc.k17751: IgM against Toxoplasma gondii is used in assessing toxoplasmosis, including in pregnancy, immunosuppression, preparation for transplantation and some congenital abnormalities. The antibodies may indicate relatively recent exposure, but their presence does not on its own prove active infection.
desc.k17793: Measures IgG to varicella-zoster virus to assess previous exposure or immunity. A single positive IgG does not confirm active chickenpox, while a negative result after vaccination may reflect the limited sensitivity of the test.
desc.k17794: Measures IgM to varicella-zoster virus. The result has limitations and does not on its own distinguish a first infection from reactivation; when skin lesions are present, PCR is usually the more suitable method for confirmation. Its use is decided according to the clinical situation.
desc.k17762: Anti-CCP helps diagnose rheumatoid arthritis and distinguish it from other autoimmune diseases with arthritis. It is requested when there is pain, swelling, stiffness and limited movement in several joints, and may give prognostic information in disease that has already been diagnosed.
desc.k17759: Anti-Jo-1 are autoantibodies that help investigate and monitor inflammatory autoimmune muscle diseases. The test is requested when signs or symptoms raise a suspicion of myositis, polymyositis or dermatomyositis, as part of a wider clinical and laboratory assessment.
desc.k17957: AMH helps assess ovarian reserve and the response of the ovaries during infertility investigations or when planning assisted reproduction. It is also used in assessing PCOS and testicular function in children, and in monitoring ovarian granulosa cell tumours; the result is related to age and the clinical context.
desc.k17765: Measures antibodies to thyroglobulin to help assess autoimmune thyroid diseases, including Hashimoto's and Graves' disease. It is interpreted with anti-TPO, TSH receptor antibodies and the clinical assessment; a negative result does not rule out disease, and the titre does not necessarily reflect disease activity.
desc.k17766: Measures antibodies to thyroid peroxidase to help identify autoimmune thyroid diseases, especially Hashimoto's and Graves' disease. The result is interpreted with hormones and other antibodies; a negative result does not rule out autoimmunity, and the antibody level does not necessarily reflect clinical activity.
desc.k17713: Anti-Xa is used to monitor anticoagulant therapy with low-molecular-weight heparin or unfractionated heparin. The measurement aims to assess the heparin level in the blood of people taking one of these therapies.
desc.k17723: The test detects autoantibodies to double-stranded DNA and is used in assessing systemic lupus erythematosus. It is requested when there are signs consistent with lupus, and in patients already diagnosed to monitor the course of the disease.
desc.k17725: Looks for LKM-1 autoantibodies against liver and kidney microsomes. The test helps diagnose autoimmune hepatitis in people with a clinical suspicion and is used to distinguish it from other forms of hepatitis, together with the overall assessment of the patient.
desc.k17756: Anti-SS-A/Ro antibodies are autoantibodies used in assessing systemic autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren's syndrome. The test is requested when symptoms suggest an autoimmune process and may serve as part of its diagnosis and monitoring.
desc.k17757: Anti-SS-B/La are autoantibodies used to help diagnose and monitor systemic autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren's syndrome. The test is requested when clinical signs raise a suspicion of these disorders and is assessed as part of the overall investigation.
desc.k29347: The test assesses antithrombin, a protein that helps naturally restrain blood clotting. It is used to investigate antithrombin deficiency when assessing thromboses, while the timing of testing after a thrombotic episode is set according to the doctor's guidance.
desc.k17575: Antibodies against insulin help assess the autoimmune process linked to type 1 diabetes, particularly in children. They are used with other markers such as GAD and IA2 to add information on risk and diagnosis, taking into account any use of insulin as a medicine.
desc.k17785: IgA endomysial antibodies (EMA) are a serological marker that helps assess coeliac disease and dermatitis herpetiformis. The test may be requested for digestive symptoms, anaemia, weight loss or other relevant signs; positive serology guides further gastroenterological assessment.
desc.k17784: IgG endomysial antibodies help assess coeliac disease, particularly in people with IgA deficiency. The test may be requested when there are digestive symptoms, anaemia, weight loss or other relevant signs; a positive result needs gastroenterological interpretation and may be followed by a biopsy.
desc.k17516: IgG antiphospholipid antibodies help investigate thrombosis, unexplained prolongation of the aPTT and recurrent pregnancy loss. The test is used with other thrombophilia parameters and, in certain cases, as part of the assessment of autoimmune diseases.
desc.k17517: IgM antiphospholipid antibodies are examined when investigating thromboses, unexplained prolongation of the aPTT and recurrent miscarriages or pregnancy complications. They are used as part of a broader assessment of clotting disorders and, sometimes, of autoimmune diseases.
desc.k17763: IgG anticardiolipin antibodies help investigate thromboses and the causes of recurrent pregnancy loss or obstetric complications. They may also be included in assessing autoimmune diseases and are interpreted together with other thrombophilia markers and clinical data.
desc.k17848: Measures IgM anticardiolipin antibodies to help investigate thromboses, recurrent miscarriages and pregnancy complications. It is included in the assessment of acquired thrombophilia and, in some cases, autoimmune diseases, and is interpreted together with other relevant antibodies and parameters.
desc.k21323: Anti-parietal cell antibodies are directed against the stomach cells that produce intrinsic factor, which is needed to absorb vitamin B12. Testing helps investigate pernicious anaemia and atrophic gastritis, where autoimmune damage can reduce the absorption of this vitamin.
desc.k17728: Looks for antibodies against sperm as part of assessing infertility due to an immunological factor. It is used before assisted fertilisation or insemination and after testicular injury, because these antibodies can affect sperm movement and fertilisation; their absence does not guarantee fertility.
desc.k17844: Measures IgG antibodies to beta2-glycoprotein as part of investigating thromboses and complications linked to acquired thrombophilia. It is used in single or recurrent thromboses and in recurrent miscarriages or obstetric complications, especially in the second or third trimester.
desc.k17845: Measures IgM antibodies to beta2-glycoprotein to help assess acquired thrombophilia. The test is used after one or more thromboses and in recurrent miscarriages or pregnancy complications, and is interpreted together with other clotting tests and relevant antibodies.
desc.k17846: Measures IgA antibodies against gliadin to help assess coeliac disease and monitor the effect of treatment. The description lists its use in chronic diarrhoea, weight loss, anaemia and in relatives of people diagnosed with coeliac disease.
desc.k17774: IgG antibodies to gliadin are used to help investigate coeliac disease and monitor the response to treatment. They are requested when there is chronic diarrhoea, weight loss or anaemia, as well as in relatives of people diagnosed with coeliac disease and in patients being monitored.
desc.k17776: Antibodies against acetylcholine receptors help diagnose myasthenia gravis, a disease that interferes with transmission from nerve to muscle. A positive result supports the clinical suspicion but is not proof on its own; a negative result does not rule out the disease, and the concentration does not always reflect the degree of muscle weakness.
desc.k17764: Antibodies to the TSH receptor help diagnose autoimmune hyperthyroidism, particularly Graves' disease. They are also used to monitor the response to therapy and assess the risk of relapse, and in the third trimester in pregnant women with a history of thyroid disease.
desc.k17579: Looks for autoantibodies to muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) in the assessment of myasthenia gravis. Identifying the MuSK-positive form helps determine the disease subtype and choose treatment, because the clinical picture may differ from the form with acetylcholine receptor antibodies.
desc.k17842: IgA antibodies to tissue transglutaminase are used to help diagnose coeliac disease and monitor treatment. They may be requested in chronic diarrhoea, anaemia, weight loss or in relatives of people diagnosed with coeliac disease.
desc.k17843: IgG antibodies to tissue transglutaminase help diagnose coeliac disease and monitor the effect of treatment. They may be requested in chronic diarrhoea, weight loss or anaemia, as well as in relatives of people with coeliac disease.
desc.k17703: APCR assesses resistance to the anticoagulant action of activated protein C. It is used in investigating thromboses, a family history of deep vein thrombosis and recurrent miscarriages or pregnancy complications, together with other thrombophilia parameters.
desc.k17384: Measures apolipoprotein A, the main protein component of HDL particles, to assess cardiovascular risk. It is interpreted with the lipid profile and other risk factors, and may be monitored during lipid-lowering treatment or after lifestyle changes.
desc.k17385: Apolipoprotein B is the main protein of LDL particles and is used to assess cardiovascular risk. It may be measured together with the lipid profile and other markers, and to monitor the response to lipid-lowering medicines or lifestyle changes.
desc.k17694: aPTT assesses blood clotting and helps investigate a deficiency of factors VIII, IX, XI or XII or the presence of clotting inhibitors. It is used to monitor unfractionated heparin, in unexplained bleeding or thromboses and as part of the assessment before procedures.
desc.k17546: ASCA IgA are antibodies to components of the wall of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The test is used to help distinguish Crohn's disease from ulcerative colitis when symptoms and other tests do not give a clear diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease.
desc.k17547: ASCA IgG are antibodies to components of the cell wall of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and help distinguish Crohn's disease from ulcerative colitis when the picture is unclear. They are not sufficient on their own for diagnosis and are not used to assess progression or response to treatment.
desc.k17285: The clinical usefulness and the test method should be confirmed by an allergist; the result does not on its own prove or rule out hypersensitivity and does not justify taking the medicine again without a specialist assessment.
desc.k17379: Measures the activity of AST, an enzyme found especially in the liver and heart, but also in muscle and other organs. It helps assess and monitor damage to liver cells, including viral hepatitis, and is interpreted together with other liver markers.
desc.k17730: ASTO measures antibodies against streptolysin O, a toxin of group A streptococci. The test helps investigate complications after infection, particularly rheumatic fever and glomerulonephritis, when there are signs of joint, heart or kidney involvement.
desc.k18231: Measures copper in the blood to assess deficiency, excess or disorders of its metabolism. It is important in investigating Wilson's disease and is assessed together with caeruloplasmin and, if needed, urinary excretion, taking into account inflammation and liver disease.
desc.k18194: Beta-2 microglobulin is used as a supporting marker for prognosis and for monitoring the response to treatment in people with diagnosed multiple myeloma or lymphoma. The result is assessed with other tests, diagnostic procedures and the full clinical picture, not in isolation.
desc.k17922: Measures beta-hCG, a placental hormone, to help confirm and monitor early pregnancy. Repeated measurements give information on its progress and may help assess an abnormal pregnancy or a possible loss, interpreted according to the stage of pregnancy.
desc.k18171: Beta-Crosslaps (beta-CTX) is a collagen fragment released during the breakdown of bone tissue and reflects bone resorption. It is used with other markers to monitor treatment of metabolic bone diseases, particularly antiresorptive therapy in osteoporosis or osteopenia.
desc.k17439: Measures bicarbonate to help assess acid–base and electrolyte balance. It is used in metabolic or respiratory disorders that may cause acidosis or alkalosis, especially when there is difficulty breathing, altered consciousness, prolonged vomiting or weakness.
desc.k17521: BNP is a peptide from the heart that rises in response to strain caused by pressure inside the heart. Measuring it helps diagnose and monitor congestive heart failure, complementing the assessment of symptoms and of the response to treatment.
desc.k17814: Western blot IgG looks for antibodies to specific proteins of Borrelia burgdorferi. It is used as a confirmatory test after a positive initial ELISA serology in investigating Lyme disease, helping to interpret exposure or infection together with clinical findings.
desc.k17880: Western blot IgM looks for antibodies to specific proteins of Borrelia burgdorferi to complement the serological diagnosis of Lyme disease.
desc.k72585: PCR looks for Borrelia burgdorferi and tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) in the same tick. The aim is to identify the pathogens present in a tick removed after contact, as information that the doctor relates to symptoms and the risk of exposure.
desc.k18270: PCR looks for Borrelia burgdorferi DNA in a tick removed from the skin, to determine whether it was carrying the cause of Lyme disease.
desc.k18007: Culture of a cervical swab looks for microorganisms that can cause inflammation of the cervix, particularly when there is discharge, itching or pelvic pain. It includes a microscopic smear and an antibiogram (antibiotic sensitivity test) when a pathogen is isolated; some sexually transmitted infections need other specific tests.
desc.k18123: The cervical swab test detects Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma and estimates their amount, with the option of testing antibiotic sensitivity. It is used when there is increased discharge, itching, burning, pelvic pain or reproductive concerns, as part of investigating microorganisms in the cervical canal.
desc.k18079: This entry refers to testing a cervical swab for Ureaplasma urealyticum. It does not explain the specific clinical purpose, method or interpretation of this test.
desc.k17974: This rapid test looks for group A streptococcal antigen in a throat swab, helping to tell whether a sore throat has a streptococcal cause. It is an indicative test: it can be positive in carriers without symptoms and negative when the amount of bacteria is low.
desc.k17975: A throat swab culture helps isolate bacteria or fungi that can cause pharyngitis. It is used for pain on swallowing, fever and swollen lymph nodes; pathogenic bacteria that are isolated are tested for antibiotic sensitivity, while fungi are reported by quantity.
desc.k17993: A nasal swab culture looks for pathogenic bacteria on the lining of the nose when a bacterial infection of the nose or sinuses is suspected. It may be used for thick discharge, small sores or a burning feeling in the nose; an antibiogram (antibiotic sensitivity test) is performed on any bacteria isolated.
desc.k18014: Looks for fungi of the genus Candida in secretions from the lining of the nose, using a nasal swab culture. The report states whether Candida was isolated and, if present, describes the amount as small, moderate or large.
desc.k18062: A skin swab culture looks for bacterial or fungal causes of surface lesions, including redness, itching and pain on the skin or in skin folds. Pathogens isolated in significant amounts are tested for antibiotic sensitivity and distinguished from the normal flora.
desc.k18064: A wound swab culture looks for bacteria or fungi that can cause infection of wounds, abscesses and deep tissues. It may be used for wounds that are not healing or that show pain, redness or pus; pathogens isolated are assessed for antibiotic sensitivity.
desc.k18105: A fungal culture of a foreskin swab looks for fungi on the glans and foreskin. It is used when there is redness, itching, a white coating, irritation, discharge or an unusual odour, and when balanitis or balanoposthitis is suspected.
desc.k17994: An eye swab culture is used to isolate bacterial or fungal causes of inflammation of the conjunctiva. It can help when there is redness, itching, burning, swollen eyelids or discharge; pathogens isolated are tested for antibiotic sensitivity.
desc.k18148: A culture of a swab from the right eye looks for bacteria or fungi that can cause inflammation of the conjunctiva. It is used when there is redness, itching, burning, swollen eyelids or discharge; when a bacterial pathogen is isolated, its antibiotic sensitivity is assessed.
desc.k18149: A culture of a swab from the left eye aims to isolate bacteria or fungi that can cause inflammation of the conjunctiva. It is used when there is burning, itching, redness, swelling or discharge; isolated pathogens may be tested for antibiotic sensitivity.
desc.k18081: A vulval swab looks for bacteria and fungi that can cause infection of the external genitals. It is used for pain, redness, swelling, itching, burning or foul-smelling discharge; when a significant number of pathogens is isolated, antibiotic sensitivity is assessed.
desc.k18010: A culture of material from the uterine cavity looks for aerobic bacteria and fungi when assessing endometritis.
desc.k18139: An anaerobic culture of a sample from the uterine cavity looks for bacteria that grow without oxygen. It helps investigate a suspected uterine infection, particularly with pelvic pain, unusual discharge, fever or persistent infections, and may be included in selected reproductive assessments.
desc.k17991: A urethral culture looks for bacterial or fungal causes of inflammation when there is discharge, itching, burning or redness. It also includes a microscopic smear for white blood cells (leucocytes) and microorganisms; when pathogens are isolated in significant amounts, an antibiogram is performed to guide treatment.
desc.k18161: The listed service is an anaerobic bacteriological examination of a urethral swab.
desc.k18057: This catalogue entry refers to testing for Mycoplasma hominis in a urethral swab. It does not specify the analytical method, clinical indications or how the result is interpreted.
desc.k18056: The service includes a direct smear from a urethral swab for Trichomonas vaginalis. It gives no details on clinical indications, test sensitivity or how the result is interpreted.
desc.k18122: This urethral swab test detects Ureaplasma and Mycoplasma hominis and estimates their amount, together with their antibiotic sensitivity. It is requested for urethral discharge, burning or frequent urination and in infertility investigations, to help identify these microorganisms in the urinary tract.
desc.k18058: This entry refers to testing for Ureaplasma urealyticum in a urethral swab.
desc.k18144: Analysis of a vaginal swab by anaerobic bacterial culture, as the test name indicates.
desc.k17979: A vaginal swab culture looks for bacteria or fungi associated with increased discharge, itching, burning, pain during intercourse or pelvic pain. It can reveal an imbalance in the microbiota; when pathogenic bacteria are isolated, an antibiogram is performed to help guide treatment.
desc.k17986: The service includes a Gram-stained direct smear from a vaginal swab.
desc.k18068: Directly examines a vaginal swab for changes in the microbiota consistent with bacterial vaginosis. It looks for fewer lactobacilli, an increase in other bacteria and “clue” cells, particularly when there is foul-smelling discharge, burning, itching or discomfort during intercourse.
desc.k18069: Examination of a direct smear from a vaginal swab for Trichomonas vaginalis, as the test name indicates.
desc.k17771: c-ANCA/anti-PR3 are autoantibodies used in diagnosing and monitoring certain autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic vasculitis. The source mentions Wegener's granulomatosis and microscopic polyangiitis, as well as occasional supporting use in distinguishing Crohn's disease from ulcerative colitis.
desc.k17926: C-peptide is released together with insulin and is used to assess how much insulin the pancreas produces. The test helps investigate hypoglycaemia and assess people with diabetes when the need for insulin or a change in treatment is being considered.
desc.k17581: Assesses the activity of C1 inactivator, a regulatory component of the complement system. It is used to investigate disorders of this system, especially when there are episodes of unexplained swelling or inflammation, frequent infections or suspected immune disorders, and to monitor the disease or its treatment.
desc.k17798: The test measures the concentration of C1 inhibitor, a protein that regulates the complement system and other processes. It helps assess a deficiency of this protein and conditions with unexplained swelling, angioedema, frequent infections or known complement disorders.
desc.k18178: CA 125 is used mainly to monitor epithelial ovarian cancer and its response to treatment, including possible recurrence. It is not recommended for population screening; levels can also rise during menstruation, pregnancy or benign conditions, so serial measurements are more informative.
desc.k18179: CA 15-3 is used mainly in patients with breast cancer to monitor the course of the disease and the response to treatment, as well as possible recurrence. It is not recommended for screening; it can also rise in benign conditions or other tumours, so serial measurements are more valuable.
desc.k18180: CA 19-9 is a tumour marker used to monitor response to treatment and detect recurrence in patients with a diagnosed pancreatic tumour. The result is assessed together with other examinations and is not interpreted in isolation from the clinical picture.
desc.k18181: CA 72-4 is used as a supporting marker to monitor treatment and detect recurrence of stomach tumours. It may also be measured in some lung, ovarian or colon tumours, before and during treatment follow-up, always together with other clinical assessment.
desc.k54951: This add-on test looks for Campylobacter spp. in the same stool sample as GI Effects. It is used to investigate diarrhoea, abdominal pain or a suspected bacterial bowel infection, including complaints after travel.
desc.k17984: Identifies the species of Candida or other yeasts and their sensitivity to five antifungals, to help choose treatment. It is important in vaginal, oral, skin or systemic infections, especially when non-albicans species may be resistant to drugs.
desc.k18182: CEA is a tumour marker used mainly in repeated measurements to monitor the course of the disease, the response to treatment or recurrence. It can rise in several types of cancer and in non-malignant conditions, so on its own it does not establish the diagnosis or the location of a tumour.
desc.k88467: Measures specific IgE to cephalosporins, according to the laboratory's description, to help identify the cause of an allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result without symptoms may indicate sensitisation; a negative result does not rule out an allergy to the drug.
desc.k17437: Measures caeruloplasmin, the main copper-carrying protein in the blood, to help investigate disorders of copper metabolism. It is used particularly when Wilson's disease is suspected, with liver or neurological signs, and is interpreted in light of the clinical picture and other tests.
desc.k17849: Assesses total complement to help investigate disorders of immune defence and monitor diseases that alter this system. It is used for recurrent bacterial infections, unexplained inflammation or swelling, suspected autoimmunity and known complement disorders.
desc.k48357: PCR looks for Chlamydia trachomatis DNA to identify urogenital infection, which can often cause no symptoms. It is used for genital complaints, screening of defined groups, investigation of infertility or pregnancy complications and checking after treatment.
desc.k17458: Cystatin C helps assess glomerular filtration and detect an early decline in kidney function. It is particularly useful when creatinine may be less informative, for example in children, older people or people with low muscle mass, and when there is a kidney risk from diabetes or hypertension.
desc.k17399: Measures creatine kinase, an enzyme that in the blood comes mainly from muscle, to detect and monitor myopathies or muscle damage. It is used when there is weakness, muscle pain or brown-coloured urine, and after damage from trauma, toxins or drugs.
desc.k17431: CK-MB is an isoenzyme of creatine kinase associated with damage to the heart muscle. It may be used for a repeat heart attack (reinfarction) or in certain cases of cardiac damage, usually together with troponin and clinical assessment.
desc.k76990: The Clostridium difficile EIA add-on test is attached to GI Effects to investigate a possible cause of diarrhoea, especially after antibiotics or a hospital stay. The description links it to gastrointestinal symptoms and changes in the microbiota; it is not offered without the base test.
desc.k17864: Measures the avidity of IgG antibodies to CMV to help distinguish a recent primary infection from an earlier one. It is particularly important during pregnancy and is interpreted together with IgG, IgM, the medical history and clinical signs.
desc.k79138: A combined test for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A/B viruses that helps clarify respiratory infections with similar symptoms. Interpretation relies on the clinical picture; a negative result does not rule out flu, and confirmation by PCR is mentioned when suspicion persists.
desc.k17745: CRP is a protein that rises during infection and inflammation and after injury or surgery. It is used to detect systemic inflammation and to monitor its course and the response to treatment, but it does not on its own identify the cause of the inflammation.
desc.k18183: Measures the marker CYFRA 21-1 to help monitor the response to treatment and recurrence of non-small cell lung cancer. The description also mentions use in some urological, gynaecological or gastrointestinal tumours, always in relation to other clinical findings.
desc.k17697: Measures D-dimer, a fragment formed when blood clots break down, which indicates activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis. It is used in assessing suspected deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism or disseminated intravascular coagulation, and in monitoring treatment of thrombosis.
desc.k46112: Analyses genetic variants in the enzymes that metabolise drugs, hormones and other compounds, as well as in antioxidant pathways. The description presents it as a profile of individual predisposition for phase I/II processes and the response to oxidative stress; it is not a diagnosis of disease.
desc.k17292: Measures diamine oxidase (DAO), an enzyme involved in breaking down histamine. Assessment requires the clinical history and the exclusion of other causes.
desc.k17288: The clinical usefulness and the test method should be confirmed by an allergist; the result does not on its own prove or rule out hypersensitivity and does not justify taking the medicine again without a specialist assessment.
desc.k17956: Dihydrotestosterone is an androgen linked to the development of the prostate and male sexual characteristics. Measuring it helps assess androgen-related disorders, including hirsutism, PCOS and disorders of testicular function; the text also mentions use in predicting the response to anti-androgen therapy in some prostate tumours.
desc.k54960: A GI Effects add-on test that looks for parasites, eggs and cysts in the stool by direct examination. It is used for prolonged gastrointestinal symptoms, travel to endemic areas or an ongoing suspicion of parasitic infection; a negative result from a single sample does not rule out infection.
desc.k17386: Direct bilirubin is used to help diagnose and monitor liver disorders, blockage of the bile ducts and, according to the source, haemolytic anaemias. It is also measured when assessing jaundice in newborns and liver-related metabolic disorders.
desc.k17832: The double test is a non-invasive first-trimester prenatal screening that combines ultrasound with free beta-hCG and PAPP-A in the mother's blood. It estimates the probability of trisomies 21, 18 and 13; it is done in weeks 11–14, most often in week 12.
desc.k25572: This genetic test looks for changes in DPYD that can reduce the activity of the enzyme dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase. It is used before or during treatment with fluoropyrimidines, such as 5-FU, capecitabine and tegafur, to assess the risk of toxicity and help choose therapy.
desc.k82021: Analyses hormones and metabolites in dried urine, including sex hormones, cortisol/cortisone, DHEA, a melatonin metabolite and selected organic acids. The component list describes what the profile measures; whether it is suitable for a clinical problem requires assessment by a doctor.
desc.k82032: Tracks changes in oestrogen and progesterone across the menstrual cycle to assess the timing of ovulation and the luteal phase. It is used as additional information for irregular cycles, cyclical symptoms such as PMS and migraine, fertility difficulties or preparation for IVF.
desc.k82046: Combines mapping of oestrogen and progesterone across the whole cycle with the DUTCH Complete profile of urinary hormones and metabolites. According to the description, it is used to assess ovulation, the luteal phase, irregular cycles and cyclical symptoms, including the cortisol rhythm and metabolic markers in the individual interpretation.
desc.k82042: This profile tracks oestrogen and progesterone across the menstrual cycle, together with the daily cortisol rhythm and the cortisol awakening response. It is described for assessing cyclical symptoms, ovulation, fertility and the link between hormonal fluctuations and stress.
desc.k82026: Combines measurements of hormones and metabolites in dried urine with salivary cortisol, including the cortisol awakening response (CAR). It provides information on the daily hormonal rhythm, sex hormones and their metabolism for the individual assessment of symptoms such as fatigue, sleep disturbances and stress-related complaints.
desc.k49084: Measures DHEA, a precursor of oestrogens and androgens, to assess hormonal disorders. It is used when adrenal dysfunction, polycystic ovary syndrome or fertility difficulties are suspected, and is interpreted according to symptoms, age and clinical history.
desc.k17916: DHEA-S is a precursor of the sex hormones, produced mainly in the adrenal glands. Measuring it helps investigate adrenal function and androgen excess, particularly in women with hirsutism, acne, irregular cycles or reproductive difficulties.
desc.k21197: eGFR-MDRD is an estimate of glomerular filtration, calculated from creatinine and demographic data. It is used to detect and monitor kidney disease, particularly in people with diabetes, hypertension, a family history of kidney disease or raised creatinine.
desc.k18268: The examination combines the physical appearance, chemical indicators and microscopic sediment of the urine. It is used in screening, in monitoring chronic kidney or liver disease and in assessing urogenital infections, giving information on the composition of the urine and its cellular elements.
desc.k17467: Faecal pancreatic elastase is used to assess the exocrine function of the pancreas, when insufficient enzyme production causes poor digestion (maldigestion). It is requested for symptoms such as weight loss, bloating or fatty stools, and to monitor people with diagnosed pancreatic insufficiency.
desc.k17582: Separates the proteins in urine to help assess proteinuria and disorders of protein production. It is used when blood proteins or albumin are altered and in investigating kidney or liver disease, multiple myeloma or plasmacytoma.
desc.k17402: Separates serum proteins to help assess changes in their amount or production. It is used when proteins/albumin are low or high and when liver or kidney disease, multiple myeloma or plasmacytoma is suspected, as well as to monitor these conditions.
desc.k17833: The ENA profile examines a group of autoantibodies to extractable nuclear antigens to help diagnose and monitor autoimmune diseases. It is requested when there are suggestive symptoms, a positive ANA result or a diagnosed autoimmune disease that is being monitored.
desc.k17946: Erythropoietin is a hormone produced mainly by the kidneys that stimulates the formation of red blood cells (erythrocytes). Measuring it helps investigate anaemia, particularly in chronic kidney disease, and primary or secondary polycythaemia, as well as assess the need for hormone replacement.
desc.k17526: Measures specific IgE to erythromycin to help investigate a suspected allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result without symptoms may indicate sensitisation only, while a negative result does not completely rule out allergy; correlation with the clinical history is required.
desc.k17918: Oestradiol helps assess ovarian function, irregular cycles, infertility and disorders of puberty. It is also used to monitor hormonal or anti-oestrogen therapy, and in men with signs of feminisation or a suspected oestrogen-producing tumour.
desc.k56854: This urinary oestrogen profile measures oestrone, oestradiol, oestriol and their metabolites to describe the level and metabolic pathways of oestrogens. The laboratory offers it for the functional assessment of hormonal balance; the metabolic ratios require clinical interpretation and do not by themselves prove the presence of disease.
desc.k17817: The test looks for Clostridium difficile toxins A and B and GDH in the stool to help investigate diarrhoea associated with this bacterium. It is especially important when unformed stools appear during or after antibiotics, chemotherapy or a hospital stay.
desc.k17972: The test looks for Helicobacter pylori antigen in the stool to help detect this microorganism, which is associated with gastritis and gastroduodenal ulcers. It is used for complaints such as upper abdominal (epigastric) pain, nausea or bloating; when the result does not match the clinical picture, other tests may be requested.
desc.k17977: A stool culture looks for microorganisms that can cause intestinal infections and describes any growth of yeasts. It is used for diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting or other digestive complaints and, in defined circumstances, to investigate carriage without symptoms.
desc.k18015: A fungal stool culture examines the presence, type and amount of fungi, especially yeasts. It is used in the context of gastrointestinal complaints or for follow-up after treatment of intestinal candidiasis; the result is assessed bearing in mind that small amounts may be part of the normal flora.
desc.k18130: The examination looks for helminth (worm) eggs in the stool to help diagnose parasitic infections. It may be used for abdominal pain, diarrhoea, weakness or weight loss; because eggs are not passed continuously, repeated samples may be needed.
desc.k18005: This rapid test looks for rotavirus and adenovirus in the stool to help identify viral gastroenteritis, particularly in children with diarrhoea and vomiting. Collecting the sample early in the illness is recommended, because the amount of antigen falls later on and may give a negative result despite infection.
desc.k18167: Bacteriological and mycological analysis of the stool examines intestinal microorganisms, dysbiosis and possible predominance of Klebsiella. According to the description, it is used to assess an imbalance of the gut flora in the context of gastrointestinal complaints; the presence of Klebsiella can be normal, while its dominance is assessed separately.
desc.k18166: The analysis combines bacteriological and mycological examination of the stool with an assessment of imbalance in the gut flora. The description focuses on changes in the ratios between microorganisms and on their overgrowth, in the context of gastrointestinal complaints and factors that alter the microbiota.
desc.k85411: The test looks for rotavirus, adenovirus, norovirus and astrovirus antigens in the stool to help identify viral gastroenteritis. It is used when there is diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain or fever; a negative result does not rule out infection, especially after the acute phase when the amount of antigen may be low.
desc.k18252: Measures the concentration of phenobarbital to help adjust the dose, assess its effect and detect toxicity. It is used at the start of therapy or after a change, when seizures continue or side effects appear, taking into account other medicines and liver/kidney function.
desc.k17435: Measures ferritin, the protein that stores iron in the body. It is used with other markers to distinguish iron-deficiency anaemia from anaemia of chronic disease, to assess iron overload and to monitor treatment.
desc.k17688: Fibrinogen is coagulation factor I, needed to form a blood clot. Measuring it helps diagnose and monitor disorders of haemostasis, particularly after thrombosis, when PT/aPTT is prolonged or an inherited abnormality is suspected, and it may be used in assessing cardiovascular risk.
desc.k17429: Measures folate to help investigate macrocytic anaemia, assess nutritional status and monitor folate deficiency. It may be requested for fatigue, weakness, pallor or relevant neurological signs.
desc.k17408: Inorganic phosphate is measured to detect or monitor disorders of the bones, kidneys and parathyroid glands that change its level. The measurement can also help monitor calcium or phosphate supplementation, usually together with vitamin D, PTH and calcium.
desc.k17406: Acid phosphatase is described as an enzyme that was used in diagnosing and monitoring prostate disease, a use now largely replaced by PSA. The text also mentions use in some bone diseases, such as Paget's disease, Gaucher disease and hyperparathyroidism, depending on the clinical situation.
desc.k17405: Measures the activity of total acid phosphatase, an enzyme found in several tissues. The description mentions its use in assessing some bone diseases, such as Paget's and Gaucher disease, and explains that its historical use for the prostate has been replaced by the more specific PSA.
desc.k17407: Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme present in several tissues, especially the liver and bone. Measuring it is used to diagnose and monitor hepatobiliary (liver and bile duct) or bone disease, usually together with AST, ALT, GGT and bilirubin when liver damage is suspected.
desc.k82132: FRAT looks for blocking and binding antibodies to folate receptor alpha, which can impair folate transport even when the blood level is normal. It serves as additional information in assessing neurological/neurodevelopmental symptoms or a suspected cerebral folate deficiency.
desc.k17937: Measures the free, biologically active fraction of testosterone, helping the assessment when total testosterone does not match the symptoms or SHBG is altered. It is used in investigating hypogonadism, infertility, puberty and hyperandrogenism in women, as well as in monitoring hormone treatment.
desc.k17942: The free beta-hCG fraction is used together with PAPP-A, ultrasound and maternal data in prenatal screening at weeks 11–14. The source also mentions the assessment of trophoblastic disease and some testicular tumours, and early follow-up after in vitro fertilisation.
desc.k18186: Free PSA is used, according to the description, to help assess tumour disease of the prostate and to monitor treatment or recurrence. It is measured in the context of urinary symptoms and other results, because tumour markers do not give an independent diagnosis.
desc.k17940: Measures the free, biologically active fraction of T3 to assess thyroid function. It is used particularly when TSH is outside the expected range or hyperthyroidism is suspected, and in monitoring hormonal disorders together with TSH and T4 or FT4.
desc.k17934: Free T4 measures the free fraction of thyroxine to assess thyroid function and to help diagnose and monitor thyroid hormone disorders. It is usually interpreted with TSH and other tests, including during pregnancy, newborn assessment or monitoring of thyroid treatment.
desc.k17489: Fructosamine reflects the binding of glucose to proteins and helps assess blood glucose levels over the last 2–3 weeks. It is used to monitor diabetes treatment or lifestyle changes, especially when HbA1c cannot be used.
desc.k17920: FSH is a pituitary hormone that supports follicle development and oestrogen production in women and sperm production (spermatogenesis) in men. Measuring it helps assess ovarian reserve and function or, together with other hormones, investigate reproductive and pituitary disorders.
desc.k17777: GAD antibodies are linked to autoimmunity against insulin-producing cells and help distinguish autoimmune type 1 diabetes from type 2. They can be detected before symptoms appear and are used for risk assessment; the text also mentions a link with some autoimmune neurological disorders.
desc.k17410: Measures the enzyme GGT and helps detect and monitor disorders of the liver and bile ducts. It is also used to clarify a rise in alkaline phosphatase and, together with carbohydrate-deficient transferrin, in assessing excessive alcohol consumption.
desc.k17620: Measures ghrelin, a hormone involved in appetite, energy metabolism and the release of growth hormone. Testing may be considered in selected assessments of weight control, hormonal balance or gastrointestinal disorders, according to the reason and timing set by the doctor.
desc.k20033: GI Effects analyses bacteria, fungi and parasites together with markers of digestion, inflammation and the gut microbiota. It is used to help investigate chronic gastrointestinal complaints; biomarkers such as calprotectin help to assess inflammation as opposed to functional disorders or dysbiosis.
desc.k17411: Glucose is measured in general health checks and to diagnose or monitor diabetes and other disorders of carbohydrate metabolism. It is used in people with risk factors, during pregnancy and to assess the effect of diabetes treatment.
desc.k51475: Measures total glutathione, which includes the reduced and oxidised forms of this cellular antioxidant. It aims to assess antioxidant defence and oxidative stress, providing additional information for individual interpretation and follow-up in the context of chronic disease.
desc.k17265: The test measures specific IgE to gluten, code f79, to help identify the trigger after an allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result indicates possible sensitisation and supports an allergy only when it matches the symptoms and the clinical assessment.
desc.k17268: The test measures specific IgE to a wasp venom component, allergen i3, after an allergic or anaphylactic reaction to a sting. A positive result may indicate sensitisation without clinical disease, while a negative result does not rule out allergy; it is interpreted together with the history of the reaction.
desc.k17559: The test determines the ABO blood group and the presence or absence of the D antigen of the Rh system. It is used before a transfusion, blood donation or surgery, during pregnancy or before conception, in preparation for a transplant, and in some forensic procedures.
desc.k18001: The test looks for blood in the stool that cannot be seen with the naked eye. It is used to screen for colorectal cancer and precancerous conditions, even without symptoms, and to help assess gastrointestinal bleeding or inflammatory bowel disease.
desc.k18027: This test looks for Demodex mites in material taken from the skin when there is redness, itching, irritation, pimples or inflammation around the eyes. The microscopic finding is combined with a dermatological examination to assess demodicosis and to guide the dermatologist's decision.
desc.k17997: Looks for pinworm (threadworm) eggs in children, in material taken from the perianal area.
desc.k54957: Detects Helicobacter pylori antigen in faeces as an add-on to GI Effects, to assess active infection. It is used for upper digestive complaints, suspected gastritis or duodenitis and to check the effect of treatment; it is not performed separately from the base test.
desc.k17440: Haptoglobin is a protein that binds free haemoglobin in the circulation. Measuring it helps diagnose and monitor haemolytic anaemias, especially when anaemia is accompanied by jaundice and there are signs of red blood cell breakdown in the body.
desc.k17401: HbA1c reflects the average blood glucose level over the previous 2–3 months by measuring haemoglobin bound to glucose. It is used as an aid in diagnosing diabetes and for periodic monitoring of glycaemic control and of whether treatment targets are being met.
desc.k18200: Total anti-HBc antibodies are part of the serological assessment of hepatitis B. Together with HBsAg and other markers, they help the doctor interpret the stage of infection when symptoms or clinical findings suggest acute or chronic hepatitis.
desc.k17394: Measures the cholesterol carried by HDL, the lipoprotein that takes excess cholesterol from the tissues to the liver. It is used together with the lipid profile to assess cardiovascular risk and to follow changes in lifestyle or lipid-lowering therapy.
desc.k18195: HE4 is used as an aid in monitoring response to treatment and detecting recurrence of epithelial ovarian cancer. It is measured before treatment and then at intervals; it is not recommended as a test for women without symptoms and is interpreted alongside other clinical findings.
desc.k17421: Measures iron as part of the assessment of anaemia or iron overload. It should be interpreted together with haemoglobin, ferritin, transferrin and TIBC/UIBC, because iron on its own does not give a complete picture of iron metabolism.
desc.k64794: The panel examines sensitisation to bee, wasp and hornet venom, including whole allergens and individual components. It is used in assessing reactions after a sting, from skin signs to systemic reactions, and is interpreted by the doctor in the clinical context.
desc.k17689: A full blood count counts the blood cells and assesses haemoglobin, haematocrit and red cell indices, together with the white cell differential. It is used for general check-ups, for investigating and monitoring anaemia, infections, inflammation and blood disorders, and for following the effects of treatments such as chemotherapy.
desc.k17601: The test measures histamine in a blood sample. The claim that it determines methylation status requires separate scientific evaluation.
desc.k18205: This combined test looks for HIV-1 p24 antigen and antibodies to HIV-1/HIV-2 to assess infection. The result depends on the time since exposure; a reactive result requires repeat testing and a confirmatory test, while an early negative result may not rule out infection.
desc.k46349: Measures holotranscobalamin, the biologically available fraction of vitamin B12, to help detect deficiency early. It is used especially where there is a risk from diet or malabsorption; interpretation can be supplemented with methylmalonic acid and homocysteine, as neurological symptoms can appear before anaemia.
desc.k17454: Homocysteine links the metabolism of methionine with folate and vitamins B6 and B12. The measurement is used to assess deficiency of these vitamins and as a marker in assessing cardiovascular risk, including coronary heart disease, stroke and peripheral arterial disease.
desc.k17923: Measures growth hormone to investigate delayed growth in children, growth hormone deficiency in adults or the excess associated with acromegaly. It may be included in the assessment of pituitary disorders and in monitoring therapy, taking into account that the hormone is secreted in pulses.
desc.k17816: hs-CRP measures low concentrations of C-reactive protein to assess chronic inflammation linked to cardiovascular risk. It is used especially in people without established disease, together with lipids and other risk markers.
desc.k17779: IA2 antibodies are markers of autoimmunity against the beta cells of the pancreas. Together with other clinical and serological markers, the measurement helps with risk assessment, diagnosis and monitoring of type 1 diabetes by looking at the process that leads to insulin deficiency.
desc.k17289: The clinical usefulness and the test method should be confirmed by an allergist; the result does not on its own prove or rule out hypersensitivity and does not justify taking the medicine again without a specialist assessment.
desc.k17545: ICA antibodies are markers of autoimmune damage to the pancreatic islet cells. The test helps assess type 1 diabetes and may be considered together with other autoantibodies, especially when the autoimmune origin of insulin deficiency needs to be clarified.
desc.k17741: Measures immunoglobulin A, a protein produced by plasma cells as part of the immune response. The test helps diagnose and monitor conditions with decreased or increased IgA, including some plasma cell disorders such as multiple myeloma.
desc.k17744: Measures total immunoglobulin E to help assess conditions with raised levels, especially allergic diseases. It is also used in the evaluation for anti-IgE therapy and when bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is suspected in patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis.
desc.k17924: IGF-1, also called somatomedin C, reflects the action of growth hormone. The measurement is used to assess abnormal growth, gigantism or acromegaly and growth hormone deficiency, and to monitor treatment in children with growth disorders.
desc.k17742: Measures the amount of immunoglobulin G, a protein produced by plasma cells as part of the immune defence. It is used to diagnose and monitor conditions with low or high IgG, including the investigation of disorders such as multiple myeloma.
desc.k17743: Measures the amount of immunoglobulin M, antibodies produced by plasma cells as part of the immune response. It is used to diagnose and monitor conditions with low or raised immunoglobulin levels and is interpreted according to the symptoms and the suspected disorder.
desc.k17404: Serum immunoelectrophoresis separates and identifies proteins to help investigate abnormal protein production. It is used when total protein or albumin is low or high, and in the assessment of liver and kidney disease, and especially of multiple myeloma and plasmacytoma.
desc.k17403: Separates and identifies urinary proteins using specific antibodies to help assess abnormal production or loss of proteins. It is used in kidney and liver disorders and especially in investigating or monitoring multiple myeloma and plasmacytoma.
desc.k17387: Indirect bilirubin is the unconjugated fraction and helps investigate jaundice, haemolysis and disorders of bilirubin processing by the liver. The value is usually calculated as the difference between total and direct bilirubin and is interpreted alongside other markers.
desc.k69406: The rapid test for influenza A and B looks for viral antigens in a nasopharyngeal sample to help diagnose flu in people with respiratory symptoms. It shows whether these types are present but does not identify subtypes; the result is interpreted in light of the overall clinical picture.
desc.k59603: The panel measures specific IgE to 54 inhaled and food allergens to help investigate an allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result may reflect sensitisation only and must be matched with clinical signs before an allergy is confirmed.
desc.k17925: Measures insulin to assess the pancreas's ability to produce it and to clarify episodes of low blood glucose. It helps investigate insulinoma and insulin resistance, and in type 2 diabetes it helps assess remaining insulin secretion and plan therapy.
desc.k17808: Interleukin-6 is a cytokine that rises during the inflammatory response to infection or tissue injury. The measurement helps assess systemic or local infections and chronic inflammatory disorders, but it is non-specific: a high value does not identify the cause and a normal value does not rule out inflammation.
desc.k17809: Interleukin-8 is a cytokine involved in attracting neutrophils, in inflammation and in tissue repair. Doctors request it as an aid in differential diagnosis and in monitoring response to treatment in chronic autoimmune or malignant diseases; as a non-specific marker, it does not on its own diagnose any particular disease.
desc.k18177: Calcitonin is a hormone produced mainly by the C cells of the thyroid and is linked to calcium and phosphorus metabolism. The measurement is particularly important in assessing medullary thyroid carcinoma, but raised levels can also occur in other tumours or diseases, including kidney failure.
desc.k17389: Calcium is measured to diagnose and monitor disorders affecting the bones, kidneys, thyroid/parathyroid glands or the digestive tract. It is also used to monitor treatment of low or high calcium, usually together with vitamin D, PTH and phosphate, depending on the clinical situation.
desc.k17388: Ionised calcium is the biologically active part of the calcium in the blood. The measurement helps assess disorders of calcium metabolism, especially at very high or very low levels and in critically ill patients, together with markers of parathyroid, kidney and bone function.
desc.k17418: Measures potassium to detect and monitor electrolyte imbalances that particularly affect the muscles, nerves and heart. It is used in check-ups, in muscle weakness or an irregular heart rhythm, and in kidney disease, high blood pressure or treatment that can change potassium levels.
desc.k17804: Faecal calprotectin is a marker of intestinal inflammation and helps distinguish inflammatory diseases from functional disorders such as irritable bowel syndrome. It is also used to assess disease activity, response to treatment and risk of relapse in inflammatory bowel disease, helping to choose further investigations.
desc.k18246: Measures the concentration of carbamazepine to monitor treatment of epilepsy, trigeminal neuralgia or bipolar disorder. It is used at the start of therapy, after a dose change, and when the effect is insufficient or toxicity is suspected, helping to balance effectiveness with safety.
desc.k43760: A peripheral blood karyotype assesses the number and structure of the chromosomes. It is used to identify chromosomal changes when investigating infertility, preparing for IVF, after recurrent early miscarriages and in conditions such as hypogonadism, amenorrhoea, azoospermia or oligospermia.
desc.k18213: Adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine are measured to help investigate catecholamine-secreting tumours and some autonomic disorders. The test relates to episodes of high blood pressure, palpitations, sweating or headache and is interpreted in the context of physiological stimuli and other tests.
desc.k18212: The test measures adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine in 24-hour urine. It is used in investigating catecholamine-secreting tumours and some autonomic disorders.
desc.k54026: The profile measures metals excreted in urine and relates the results to creatinine to account for how dilute the sample is. The laboratory offers it to assess exposure and to monitor the elimination of metals, with or without provocation, and it requires interpretation in light of the clinical history and treatment.
desc.k17392: Chloride helps assess fluid balance and acid–base status, usually together with sodium, potassium and bicarbonate. The test is used in routine check-ups and to diagnose or monitor kidney, heart and adrenal diseases that can cause electrolyte disturbances.
desc.k54954: This GI Effects add-on test looks for yeasts and fungi by microscopy of faeces after treatment with KOH. It helps assess their presence in the context of dysbiosis and gastrointestinal complaints, using the sample from the base profile.
desc.k17498: Measures prothrombin time to assess blood clotting and to monitor treatment with vitamin K antagonists. It is used in unexplained bleeding or thrombosis, deficiency or inhibition of clotting factors, assessment of liver function and preparation before procedures.
desc.k17693: Thrombin time helps assess fibrinogen function and investigate clotting disorders. It is requested in unexplained bleeding or thrombosis, prolonged clotting times, suspected low fibrinogen levels or function, or heparin contamination.
desc.k17393: Total cholesterol helps assess cardiovascular risk and monitor the effect of lipid-lowering treatment. It is usually reviewed as part of the lipid profile with HDL, LDL and triglycerides, because excess cholesterol can build up in the walls of blood vessels.
desc.k17396: Measures cholinesterase activity to help investigate poisoning by or prolonged exposure to organophosphates and to assess the liver's capacity to make proteins. It may also be requested when an inherited variant of the enzyme is suspected, linked to prolonged apnoea or paralysis after succinylcholine.
desc.k17735: C3 is part of the complement system, which helps defend against pathogens and clear damaged cells. The measurement is used in investigating recurrent infections, inflammation or autoimmune diseases, and in monitoring known complement disorders and response to treatment.
desc.k17736: C4 is a component of innate immune defence and is measured when investigating autoimmune diseases, recurrent infections or complement disorders. Together with C3 it helps assess lupus and immune complex diseases; a low level may be linked to consumption or an inherited deficiency.
desc.k49845: Measures cortisol in the blood to help investigate increased or decreased production by the adrenal glands, including suspected Cushing's syndrome or Addison's disease. Interpretation depends on the symptoms and the time the sample was taken, because the concentration varies naturally during the day.
desc.k17586: Measures cortisol excreted in urine collected over 24 hours; cortisol is a hormone of the adrenal cortex with a role in metabolism and the stress response. The test is used in assessing disorders of cortisol production, including Cushing's syndrome and Addison's disease.
desc.k43455: Data on the hormonal rhythm do not on their own determine the cause of fatigue, stress or sleep disorders.
desc.k17397: Measures creatinine, a product of muscle metabolism that is removed by the kidneys, to assess kidney function. It is used in check-ups, when kidney disease or a condition affected by poor kidney function is suspected, and to monitor progress and response to treatment.
desc.k17954: Chromogranin A is an aid in diagnosing carcinoids and neuroendocrine tumours and in monitoring response to treatment. It is requested in people with possible signs such as facial flushing, diarrhoea or difficulty breathing and is interpreted together with other investigations.
desc.k17482: Measures lactate, a product of energy metabolism that can build up when it is produced faster than it is used or cleared. The result is relevant to conditions such as shock, sepsis, heart failure or metabolic disorders, while intense physical activity can cause a temporary rise.
desc.k18247: Measuring lamotrigine in the blood helps assess the effectiveness and safety of treatment, especially in epilepsy. It is used at the start of therapy, after a dose change, and when toxicity or an interaction with other medicines is suspected; liver and kidney function and other medicines being taken affect interpretation.
desc.k17395: Measures the cholesterol carried by LDL, which is linked to the development of atherosclerosis. It is used as part of the lipid profile to assess cardiovascular risk and to check the response to lipid-lowering treatment or other measures to manage this risk.
desc.k17412: LDH is an enzyme found in many tissues and serves as a non-specific marker of cell damage. It is used in assessing haemolysis, liver or kidney disease and some tumours, and in comparing blood with body fluids when investigating fluid collections.
desc.k17456: Measures leptin, the hormone linked to fat tissue, appetite and energy balance. The test is used in the assessment of obesity, metabolic, eating or endocrine disorders and menstrual cycle and fertility problems, together with other investigations.
desc.k18250: Measuring levetiracetam in the blood helps tailor epilepsy treatment and assess its effectiveness or possible toxicity. It is used especially at the start of treatment, after a dose change, when seizures are not controlled or when side effects appear.
desc.k17921: Measures luteinising hormone to assess pituitary, ovarian or testicular function. It is used in infertility, menstrual cycle and ovulation disorders, in men with a low sperm count or reduced libido, and in children with early or delayed puberty, usually together with other hormones.
desc.k17528: Measures specific IgE to lidocaine/Xylocaine to help assess a suspected allergic or anaphylactic reaction. A positive result indicates sensitisation and supports an allergy only if it matches the symptoms; a negative result does not completely rule it out.
desc.k43570: The PCR looks for the genetic material of the mpox (monkeypox) virus in the sample taken. It is used for laboratory confirmation when the doctor suspects infection from the symptoms and lesions; the quality and type of sample affect the reliability of the result.
desc.k17413: Lipase is a digestive enzyme; measuring it is used to diagnose and monitor acute pancreatitis. It may be requested in severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, and is interpreted according to when the symptoms started and the clinical condition.
desc.k17447: Lp(a) is a lipoprotein linked to atherosclerosis and thrombosis, used to assess cardiovascular risk. It is particularly relevant when there is a family history of early cardiovascular disease, or disease or a heart attack that is not well explained by traditional risk factors.
desc.k17414: Measures lithium during treatment to check whether exposure to the medicine is appropriate and to assess toxicity. Interpretation takes into account the dose, kidney function, hydration, salt in the diet and other medicines, because the margin between a therapeutic and a toxic effect is narrow.
